primary.name: Chronic Kidney Disease with Volume Overload

encounters.cc: Increasing fatigue, decreased appetite, and mild ankle swelling over the past 4 months.

lines: Increasing fatigue, decreased appetite, and mild ankle swelling over the past 4 months.
He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or changes in urination.
He notes occasional lightheadedness when standing and has unintentionally lost 4 pounds in the past few months.
- History of Ischemic Stroke with full recovery
He has a history of hypertension, managed with multiple medications.
His medication list includes a thiazide diuretic, amlodipine, and low-dose aspirin.
Family history is notable for stroke in his brother and type 2 diabetes in his daughter.
He does not smoke or drink alcohol.
On exam, blood pressure is 152/88 mm Hg, pulse is 72/min, and BMI is 26.
Cardiovascular and pulmonary exams are unremarkable.
Urinalysis shows 1+ protein, no hematuria, and bland sediment.
Renal ultrasound reveals bilaterally echogenic kidneys measuring ~9.4 cm each.

encounters.cc: Fever, sore throat, and rash on his chest and arms.

lines: Fever, sore throat, and rash on his chest and arms.
The patient is an 82-year-old male with chronic kidney disease who returns eight months after evaluation for volume overload.
He presents with a 5-day history of fever, sore throat, rash on his chest and arms, muscle aches, fatigue, and mild headache.
- Chronic Kidney Disease with Volume Overload (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of Ischemic Stroke with full recovery
Who lives in a shared nursing facility
On examination, he has nonexudative pharyngitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, and a faint maculopapular rash scattered across his chest and upper arms.
A rapid strep test and monospot test are both negative. An HIV ELISA is ordered.

encounters.cc: Severe pain, redness, and swelling in his right great toe for 3 days.

lines: Severe pain, redness, and swelling in his right great toe for 3 days.
The patient with CKD stage 3b, previously managed for volume overload, presents with severe toe pain.
The pain began abruptly at night and worsened over the next 48 hours, making it difficult for him to walk.
Two years ago, he had a similar episode in his left foot that resolved with treatment.
- Chronic Kidney Disease with Volume Overload (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of Ischemic Stroke with full recovery
He has a history of hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and hyperlipidemia.
He takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and low-dose aspirin daily.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired postal worker.
On examination, the metatarsophalangeal joint of the right great toe is markedly tender, warm, and erythematous with restricted range of motion.
The patient is started on colchicine.

encounters.cc: Collapsed while walking up a flight of stairs.

lines: Collapsed while walking up a flight of stairs.

This 85-year-old with severe aortic stenosis and chronic kidney disease, evaluated in 2020 for volume overload, is brought to the emergency department by his daughter because he collapsed while walking up a flight of stairs.
Over the past few months, he has experienced progressive fatigue and exertional chest tightness.
- Chronic Kidney Disease with Volume Overload (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of Ischemic Stroke with full recovery
His medical history includes hyperlipidemia and mild chronic kidney disease.
He does not smoke or drink alcohol.
On examination, his blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg, pulse is 72/min and regular, and respirations are 16/min
Carotid upstroke is slow and delayed.
Auscultation reveals a murmur that radiates to the neck.

encounters.cc: Progressive confusion and lethargy over the past 3 days.

lines: Progressive confusion and lethargy over the past 3 days.
This 86-year-old with aortic stenosis, chronic kidney disease, and remote intravenous drug use returns after his 2023 ED visit.
His daughter says he has been “not himself” and seemed weaker than usual after a recent family dinner.
She recalls no head trauma or sick contacts, though he did complain of some mild abdominal cramps the day before presentation.
- Chronic Kidney Disease with Volume Overload (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of Ischemic Stroke with full recovery
His past history includes hypertension, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and a remote ischemic stroke with full recovery.
He takes aspirin and a thiazide.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired postal worker.
On arrival, his temperature is 38.5 °C (101.3 °F), blood pressure is 138/76 mm Hg, pulse is 94/min, and respiratory rate is 18/min.
Physical examination shows an elderly man with disorientation, mild nuchal rigidity, and photophobia.
There are no focal motor deficits, and fundoscopic exam is normal.
A lumbar puncture is performed, and CSF studies show: Opening pressure Elevated Appearance Cloudy WBC count 1200/µL (90% neutrophils) Protein 210 mg/dL Glucose 25 mg/dL
CT scan of the head shows age-related atrophy but no acute bleed.
This organism is characterized by entering the body through the gastrointestinal tract after contaminated food ingestion.
